title: Orsen and the Postcards
author: Rosalind Ashgrove
blurb: Quentin Dravenmoor, a translator losing a childhood language one borrowed word at a time, has spent twelve years practicing the art of almost saying it. Then a box of undelivered letters surfaces behind a wardrobe — and she is pulled straight into the middle of it. To get through this, she must translate the untranslatable sentence and live with it before the demolition date arrives.
style: crisp modern voice, short chapters, propulsive momentum
